summary.headline: TD Power Systems FY26 standalone PAT rose 42% to INR2.18bn; FY27 revenue guided at INR24bn-plus, with a Turkey LD penalty dragging Q4 margins.
summary.overview: FY26 standalone total income rose 35% to INR17.37bn and PAT rose 42% to INR2.18bn; consolidated PAT rose 36% to INR2.36bn. Full-year order inflow was INR22.38bn (+51%), with exports at 79%, and the manufacturing order book stood at INR19.73bn at year-end. Q4 consolidated gross contribution margin fell about 3 points below the 33-34% historical average because of a one-off Turkey contract penalty after components shipped from India were delayed about 1.5 months. Management revised FY27 revenue guidance to INR2,400-plus crore and flagged a large-generator capacity expansion (rotors, machining up to about 200 MW) with details deferred about 2-3 months.

segments.name: Generators (gas turbine and gas engine)
segments.commentary: Largest order-book component at INR16.77bn; management describes large volume orders for sub-50 MW units, with FY28 forecasts still rising. Notable deliveries cited include SpaceX. Pending orders for generators and motors grew 66% in FY26.

segments.name: Steam turbines
segments.commentary: About 25% of revenue per management. Domestic market expected to grow 10-12%, driven by captive, biomass and waste-heat recovery, with unit sizes moving from 30 MW to 60 MW.

segments.name: Hydro
segments.commentary: Management expects FY26 to be one of its highest years in hydro, with high-value refurbishment order wins expected in Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Motors
segments.commentary: Management is separating motor manufacturing lines after prioritising generators during FY26, expecting the segment to stabilise and traction to improve.

segments.name: Railway
segments.commentary: Order book INR2.47bn. Supplying to US, Europe and Russia, plus India, which management counts as four markets next year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance revised to INR2,400-plus crore (about INR24bn), with management signalling an extremely high probability of raising it further to match order inflow.
FY28 capacity from current facilities plus planned capex is about INR30-32bn; management says FY28 numbers are conservative.
Order book growth of 20-25% expected in FY28 on a conservative basis; all pending order book of about INR2,000 crore to be executed in FY27.
Q1 FY27 execution expected to beat Q4 FY26.
Consolidated gross contribution margin expected to revert to the historical 33-34% average; no similar shipping exposure expected.
Margins expected to remain broadly stable for the next 2-3 quarters despite commodity inflation, with hedges and price variation clauses providing a buffer.
Large-generator capacity complete by calendar 2027; large ramp-up in calendar 2028 (FY29); commitments made to the market from FY29.
capex_capacity: Large-generator expansion: management plans heavy investment in rotor manufacturing and large machining (up to about 200 MW). Amount not disclosed; details to follow in about 2-3 months.
Machine lead time for large machining equipment is 15-16 months, so full capacity is earliest in calendar 2027.
Routine capex of about INR50 crore in FY27 for bottleneck debottlenecking and small capacity additions, with a similar amount in FY28 for automation.
Current capacity and planned capex support about INR30-32bn of sales through FY28.
Turkey plant serves the Turkish market and acts as a backup and service shop for Europe.
demand_pricing: Management described the market as very buoyant across segments, driven by AI data centres, grid stabilisation, power generation and renewables.

Turbine and engine OEMs plan to roughly double capacity by 2030, and generator demand follows prime-mover capacity. Management said the Western and Japanese large-generator competitors include Siemens, Baker Hughes (Brush), Mitsubishi, Fuji Electric and Toshiba.

Pricing: management said it is hard to get better prices than current levels; currency tailwinds and raw material price variation clauses are in place, but TDPS will not earn the margins turbine OEMs earn.

Commodity inflation: copper is about USD14,000 per tonne, hedges are running out, and customers' price increases are approaching double digits. Rupee depreciation offsets this as an export-led business.
Nuclear: NPCIL ordering is slow and choppy, and competition includes BHEL, Crompton and imports.
Management said some customer prices are not yet in effect, creating a lag in price recovery.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 gross margin contract, and will it revert?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated gross contribution margin averages 33-34% (about 34%); Q4 was about 3 points lower because a Turkey contract was delayed about 1.5 months by components stuck on a shipment from India, and a high LD penalty was paid. Management expects a return to historical levels.

qa_highlights.question: Commodity and currency impact on margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Copper price increases are running off hedges and customer price increases are only partly in effect; rupee depreciation is expected to offset this. Management expects broad neutrality for 2-3 quarters but said a further 20-30% commodity rise would need a response.

qa_highlights.question: Large-generator capex, end markets and timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed capacity expansion in rotors and large machining; quantum and ramp-up to be disclosed in about 2-3 months. End markets are mainly export: power generation, AI data centres and combined-cycle applications. Full capacity is earliest in calendar 2027, with the big ramp in calendar 2028.

qa_highlights.question: Execution risk from turbine OEMs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the opposite: turbine and engine customers monitor deliveries twice weekly and take machines immediately, so the pressure is on TDPS execution. No machines are waiting in the shop on the gas side.

qa_highlights.question: Trade receivables growing faster than sales; EBITDA-to-CFO conversion at 21%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the outstanding amount of about INR700 crore that was due has been fully covered. Working capital is building for growth, and the company expects conversion to improve as inventory turns into cash next quarter. Management said retained earnings are going into working capital.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 revenue and FY28 capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 guidance is INR2,400-plus crore. Current and planned capacity covers about INR30-32bn through FY28, which management calls conservative. Order book growth of 20-25% is expected in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new CEO a large-generator hire?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed a new CEO, Deepak, joined as number two, and is not only for the large-generator business. He previously was at L&T Mitsubishi and GE. Deepak did not join the call.

risks_watch: Q4 consolidated gross margin fell about 3 points below the 33-34% average, due to the Turkey penalty; watch Q1 FY27 margin recovery.
Commodity inflation: copper near USD14,000, hedges running out, and pass-through lag; a further 20-30% commodity spike would require action per management.
High factory utilisation raises breakdown and delay risk; management calls this the new normal.
Large-generator capex amount and business plan are undisclosed, with machine lead times of 15-16 months; ramp is not before calendar 2027-28.
Working capital intensity: receivables are growing faster than sales and EBITDA-to-CFO conversion was about 21%.
Customer concentration and capacity agreement with INNIO are undisclosed in detail; management declined to quantify share of wallet.
Motor segment is still recovering, with lines being separated after being deprioritised in FY26.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and order inflow, with clear execution focus. Evasive on specifics: it declined to size the large-generator capex, name customers, quantify INNIO share of wallet, give steam/gas revenue split, or comment on aeroderivative prototypes, deferring to a call in about 2-3 months.
